title: One-off credit slope and usage scenarios
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Rough, personal scratchpad for a one-off credit design that reduces onboarding friction but limits abuse. Not a spec; just math and scenarios to jog product conversations.

High-level idea:
- Give a small, single-use credit bundle on signup that decays over 30 days and is tailored by signal (email verified, first integration step completed). Use credits to subsidize early API calls / chat sessions.
- Credits are consumed by a weighted token model: base token unit + latency-sla multiplier for real-time routes.

Assumptions (back of envelope):
- amortized infra cost per 1M tokens served (generation) = $6.00 (includes GPU, network, storage, infra ops) -> base cost per token = $6 / 1,000,000 = $0.000006
- desired early-subsidy hit rate: allow free-ish experience up to $3 of infra cost per new user within first 30 days
- conversion target: users who consume >$20 infra in 90 days convert to trial-to-paid path at 5% uplift

Credit sizing options:
1) Flat credit: $3 infra credit (equivalent tokens = 3 / 0.000006 = ~500k tokens)
   - Pros: simple, easy to advertise
   - Cons: hero users can burn quickly with embedding/search workloads
2) Session-bucketed credit: 10 session credits, each session = up to 5k tokens (50k tokens total) -> approx $0.30
   - Pros: forces distributed exploration; protects backend from single-run burn
   - Cons: complicated UX, must define session boundary heuristics
3) Mix: $1 flat + 5 session tokens * 10k tokens (50k) -> balances exploration and protection

Token weighting and route multipliers (proposal):
- base gen token weight = 1x (cost = $0.000006)
- embedding token weight = 4x (if embedding unit ~ 10x cost per token because offline indexing cost) -> effectively $0.000024 per token-equivalent
- real-time low-latency route surcharge = 1.5x credit burn (we want to subsidize costlier SLOs less)
- example: 1k gen tokens on low-latency chat = 1k * 1x * 1.5 = 1500 token-equivalents -> credit cost $0.009

Example user archetypes (how credits get used):
- Explorer (chat-first): opens web chat, runs 10 short experiments, avg 800 tokens/experiment = 8k tokens -> uses ~8k token-eq -> trivial cost (~$0.048).
- Integrator (embedding-heavy): uploads dataset, runs 5 embeddings of 5k tokens each -> 25k embedding tokens -> token-eq 25k*4=100k -> cost ~$0.60 -> eats embedding budget fast.
- Automator (large-batch calls): runs a 500k token batch job -> cost ~$3 -> eats entire $3 flat credit if available.

SLA & UX constraints:
- Credits should not be allowed for Paid-Only features (dedicated capacity routes, private VPC on-prem installs).
- UI: show "credit burn bar" per feature (gen vs embeddings). Avoid too many decimals; show human-friendly units ("~500k tokens remaining").

Decay and expiry rules (sketch):
- Credits valid for 30 days, prorated window from signup trigger.
- If user completes key activation steps (billing added OR first paid commit), convert remaining credits into a small onboarding discount code (non-transferable).
- Fraud control: rate-limit per-account embedding concurrency while under credit subsidy. Flag unusual bursts to the fraud queue.

Unit economics quick check (cohort-level):
- If 1000 signups get $3 credit each -> subsidy exposure = $3,000 in infra cost.
- Expected conversion to paid = 3% (30 customers). If ARPU first-year target = $2,000 per converting customer -> revenue = $60k.
- Payback: $60k - $3k subsidy = $57k gross, but need to subtract CAC, ops, etc. So subsidy seems low relative to one large cohort winner, but we should model realistic conversion.

Alternative knobs (for experimentation):
- Activity-gated credits: only give full credit when email verified + first API call + integration step 1. Reduces lurkers.
- Progressive unlock: give 50% upfront, remaining 50% after performing a follow-up action (invite teammate, create dataset).
- Regional scaling: lower credit in high-cost regions (where infra cost per token is 20–40% higher).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to measure "session" reliably for web vs API? Proxy heuristics: 10 minute inactivity OR explicit start/stop event. Need SRE input.
- Should we separate credits per product vertical (chat vs embeddings) to prevent cross-exhaustion?
- What is true average embedding cost for real customer datasets (needs infra sampling across corpora)?
- UX copy: what phrasing minimizes expectation of "free forever" and nudges to try paid features? Draft candidates needed.

Small experiment proposal (2 weeks):
- A/B test two variants across 10k new signups each: (A) $3 flat credit, (B) $1 flat + 5 session-credits. Measure: 14-day retention, 30-day usage distribution (gen vs embed), conversion at 90 days.
- Track anomaly queue: percentage of accounts that exceeded 2x expected burn per archetype -> flag for manual review.

Quick notes to self:
- Revisit assumed infra cost per 1M tokens with infra team (I guessed $6; could be +-50%).
- Discuss embedding weight with research (indexing/storage durability costs not captured here).
- Pull historical signup-to-first-bill conversion numbers from growth dashboard (needed to model subsidy ROI).

End of scratchpad.

(very rough — will turn into a PRD sketch once figs and infra inputs validated)
